1.why: All six screens show a static, uncluttered layout with no animations, carousels, auto-play media or pop-up dialogs.

2.why: Primary actions use high-contrast blue buttons and bold headings that stand out from body text and the secondary Stay-safe/Logs panels.

3.why: Each step presents a single obvious form and button in the main card, making the next required action easy to locate.

4.why: The flow requires the user to handle an email/reference, a long hex recovery code, a separate MFA code and a privacy checkbox, so several items must be remembered or transcribed.

5.why: No password-manager hints, autofill attributes, 'remember me' checkboxes or similar assistive options appear on any screen.

6.why: Apart from the pre-filled test recovery code on step 2, the interface never surfaces previously saved or familiar credentials for recognition.

7.why: Labels and instructional sentences are concise, use plain language and are rendered in a highly legible font size and contrast.

8.why: No error states or error messages are shown in any of the six screenshots, so the claim that errors describe the problem and fix cannot be verified as true.

9.why: Step 2 explicitly displays a sample recovery code and a 'Use the recovery link' affordance; the Logs panel also surfaces the MFA code as a concrete example.

10.why: The only authentication path offered is typed recovery/MFA codes; no alternative choices such as password, passkey or face login are presented.

11.why: Each screen contains exactly one primary decision or input, never a large set of simultaneous options.

12.why: Success feedback is given after every step (banner text, green completion message, and real-time log lines confirming each verification).

13.why: Generic 'Stay safe' tips are repeated on every page, yet contextual short help or inline tips for the specific new action are minimal.

14.why: Nothing prevents re-submission of a form, but no explicit 'try again', edit or back controls are visible to simplify recovery from a mistake.

15.why: Header, card layout, button style, Stay-safe block and Logs panel remain visually and structurally identical across all steps.
